title: Toasted Pecan Buttermilk Pancakes
changes_from_base: A smaller, thinner batter of buttermilk and milk with no soured cream, the egg white whisked into the milk, and finely chopped toasted pecans folded through.
summary: Buttery buttermilk pancakes flecked with toasted pecans, cooked on a hot griddle until golden.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
milk, plus about 1 tbsp more if the batter is too thick

steps.title: Mix Dry
steps.text: Mix 142 g plain flour, 2 tsp caster sugar, ½ tsp fine salt, ½ tsp baking powder and ¼ tsp bicarbonate of soda in a bowl.

steps.title: Mix Wet
steps.text: Pour 180 ml buttermilk and 120 ml milk into a jug and whisk in the egg white, then stir the yolk mixed with 28 g melted butter into the milk.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet mixture into the dry all at once and whisk until just mixed, then fold in 30 g toasted chopped pecans, loosening with up to 1 tbsp extra milk if the batter seems thick.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat a griddle or large frying pan over a strong medium-high heat and brush generously with vegetable oil until a splash of water sizzles hard.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour about 60 ml batter per pancake without crowding the pan and cook until the bases are brown and the tops start to bubble, 2-3 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook until browned, a further 1-2 min, oiling the pan again before each new batch.

tips: Toast the pecans first so their flavour comes through in every bite.
Test the griddle with a splash of water - it should sizzle hard before you add batter.
Loosen the batter with a little extra milk if it feels too thick to spread.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
